pk.context: 80 mg oral, single dose, healthy adults

clues.kinetics: Absolute bioavailability of the parent drug is about 14%, and food changes absorption only modestly. It is at least 98% bound to plasma proteins and is cleared mainly by hepatic metabolism and biliary elimination.
clues.substance: A calcium salt trihydrate, crystalline and insoluble in aqueous solutions at pH 4 or below. The active moiety has a molecular weight of 558.6.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as tablets of 10, 20, 40 and 80 mg.
clues.safety: Contraindicated in acute liver failure, decompensated cirrhosis and hypersensitivity to the drug; no boxed warning. Myalgia and diarrhea are the commonest reactions leading to discontinuation.
clues.indication: Reducing heart attack, stroke, revascularization and angina in adults with coronary risk factors, and lowering LDL cholesterol in primary hyperlipidemia or familial hypercholesterolemia.
clues.mechanism: A selective, competitive inhibitor of HMG-CoA reductase, the enzyme that makes mevalonate, a cholesterol precursor. It raises liver LDL receptors, so more LDL is taken up and cleared.

tell: Only about 14% of the parent drug reaches the circulation, yet LDL-C lowering is the same with or without food.
